How does selling a house work across Pennsylvania's 67 counties?

Selling a house in Pennsylvania means dealing with local government that is split into many small pieces. The state has 67 counties, and Philadelphia County shares its boundaries with the City of Philadelphia. Below the county level sit 2,555 municipalities: 1,545 townships, 953 boroughs, 56 cities and one town, Bloomsburg.

That matters because a mailing address does not always name the local government. A Lancaster address might sit in Manheim Township or East Hempfield Township, and the county, township and school district each play a part.

Three offices come up in almost every sale:

  • The county assessment office, which sets the assessed value and handles homestead applications.
  • The county Recorder of Deeds, which records the deed and collects transfer tax.
  • The county Register of Wills, which opens estates when a house comes from someone who has died.

What does a Pennsylvania seller pay at closing in transfer tax?

The state realty transfer tax is 1 percent of the value of the real estate, and it applies to deeds and other written transfers. Local governments may add their own transfer tax on top, so the total depends on where the house sits. Ask the county recorder for the local rate.

Both the grantor and the grantee are jointly and severally liable for the tax. In plain terms, the state can collect it from either side, so the contract should say who pays and the settlement statement should show it. County Recorders of Deeds collect the tax, often together with any local tax, and send the state share to the Department of Revenue.

ItemWhat the state says
State realty transfer tax1 percent of value
Local transfer taxAllowed; set by the locality
Who is liableGrantor and grantee jointly
Who collectsCounty Recorder of Deeds
Transfers that can be exemptCertain family transfers, transfers by testate or intestate succession, transfers to government

How do property taxes and the homestead exclusion work?

Property tax in Pennsylvania is a local matter. Counties assess, and the county, municipality and school district each levy their own tax.

The homestead exclusion is a school tax reduction for a primary residence. The Department of Community and Economic Development says only a primary residence qualifies, and that the assessed value of each approved homestead is reduced by the same amount before the tax is figured. The application goes to the county assessment office, and to receive relief for a tax year the application must be filed by the preceding March 1.

If you are selling a house you no longer live in, do not assume the exclusion is still active. Ask the assessment office whether the exclusion is on the parcel, because a buyer who will rent the house may not qualify. Our state guides cover the homestead exclusion, the Property Tax/Rent Rebate program and the full Pennsylvania property tax guide.

Is foreclosure judicial in Pennsylvania, and what are the deadlines?

Yes. Pennsylvania mortgage foreclosure is judicial, so the lender has to file a lawsuit and win a judgment before the house can be sold at a sheriff's sale.

The Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency explains the notice that starts the clock. A lender must send an Act 91 notice, and the notice sets out two windows:

  • 33 days from the date of the notice to meet face to face with an approved consumer credit counseling agency if you want to apply for HEMAP, the state's Homeowner's Emergency Mortgage Assistance Program.
  • 30 days from the date of the notice to pay the amount listed and cure the default.

The notice also says a homeowner may cure up to one hour before a sheriff's sale, up to three times in a calendar year. According to a legal summary from Nolo, the sale notice must be posted on the property and served on the owner at least 30 days before the sale, and Pennsylvania has no redemption period after the sale. Under federal rules a servicer generally cannot start a foreclosure until a loan is more than 120 days past due.

If a sale date is already set, selling before it happens can protect your credit and any equity. See our guide to the Pennsylvania sheriff sale process and our page on tax sales.

What happens when you sell an inherited house in Pennsylvania?

Start with the county Register of Wills. That office opens the estate and issues the grant of letters to the executor or administrator. Berks County explains that it also issues short certificates, which are the copies a title company or bank usually asks to see before an estate asset is sold. Berks County notes its clerks cannot give legal advice.

Inheritance tax is a separate step with its own deadlines. The Department of Revenue lists these rates:

  • 0 percent for a surviving spouse, and for a parent inheriting from a child aged 21 or younger.
  • 4.5 percent for direct descendants and lineal heirs.
  • 12 percent for siblings.
  • 15 percent for other heirs, with charities and government entities exempt.

Tax is due at death and becomes delinquent nine months later. A 5 percent discount applies if it is paid within three months of death. Since January 16, 2026, an estate with no familial heirs passes first to an endowed community fund in the municipality, then the school district, then the county, and only then to the Commonwealth.

Our probate guide and inheritance tax guide go deeper.

What must a seller disclose about the condition of the house?

Pennsylvania's Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law requires a seller of residential property with one to four dwelling units to give the buyer a signed and dated property disclosure statement. It has to reach the buyer before the seller and buyer sign the agreement of transfer. If something on the form becomes inaccurate before settlement, the seller must tell the buyer.

The Real Estate Commission form asks about the roof, basement and crawl spaces, pests, structural problems, water and sewage systems, plumbing, heating, electrical, soils and drainage, hazardous substances, homeowners association matters and legal issues affecting title. The seller does not have to investigate, but cannot state something known to be false or hide a known material defect.

Some transfers are exempt, including those by a fiduciary administering a decedent's estate, guardianship or trust, and transfers to a mortgagee or foreclosure buyer after default. A buyer who believes a seller broke the law generally has two years after final settlement to sue.

A cash sale as is does not wipe out this duty when it applies. It means the buyer takes the house in its present condition and the seller does not repair or credit for repairs.

Which property problems come up most often for Pennsylvania sellers?

Radon is the one the state asks homeowners to check. The Department of Environmental Protection says about 40 percent of Pennsylvania homes have radon levels above the EPA action level of 4.0 pCi/L, and that the state's geology makes elevated levels more likely. Any house can be affected, so testing is the only way to know.

Radon factDEP figure
Homes above the 4.0 pCi/L action levelAbout 40 percent
Typical test kit costAbout $20 to $30
Typical mitigation system costAbout $800 to $1,200

We buy houses as is. For a rental, read Pennsylvania landlord and tenant law and eviction notice rules before you talk to the tenants. We do not summarize lease law here, so check the lease and ask a local attorney how a sale affects the tenancy.

Who closes a sale in Pennsylvania, and where do you start?

The deed is recorded with the county Recorder of Deeds. Ask whoever handles your closing, whether a title company or an attorney, to confirm the transfer tax and the payoff figures for any liens.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Pennsylvania have?

Pennsylvania has 67 counties. Philadelphia County and the City of Philadelphia cover the same area. Each has its own recorder and assessment office.

What is the Pennsylvania realty transfer tax?

The state tax is 1 percent of the value of the property. Localities may add their own, and the county Recorder of Deeds collects both. The grantor and grantee are jointly liable, so the contract should say who pays.

Is Pennsylvania foreclosure judicial?

Yes. The lender files a lawsuit and gets a judgment before a sheriff's sale. An Act 91 notice gives 33 days to meet with a credit counseling agency about HEMAP and 30 days to cure the default.

Can I sell a house I inherited before probate ends?

The executor usually needs letters from the county Register of Wills before signing a deed for estate property. Ask the Register of Wills what your case requires.

Do I need to give a disclosure statement?

Sellers of one to four unit residential property generally must give a signed statement before the agreement of transfer is signed. Transfers by estate fiduciaries and foreclosure transfers are among the exemptions.

What does selling as is mean?

The buyer takes the house in its current condition and the seller makes no repairs.

Does the homestead exclusion transfer to the buyer?

No. It is tied to an owner's primary residence and an application filed with the county assessment office. The buyer must apply on their own.
